doNow.prompt: A pupil says: plants take food from the soil through their roots, like we eat food. What is wrong with this idea?

choices.text: Nothing: the roots are the mouth of the plant and eat food from the soil
choices.misconception: Plants take food from the soil through their roots, like we eat food.

rationale.chose: The learner selected option Nothing: the roots are the mouth of the plant and eat food from the soil as their answer to this question.
rationale.thinks: They are applying the coded wrong turn instead of following the water from the roots up the stem to the leaves to check where the plant really makes its food.
rationale.reteach: Reteach from the paired notes trap: Plants take food from the soil through their roots, like we eat food.. We eat through our mouths, so the roots look like a mouth for the plant. Roots drink water and minerals; the leaves make the food with sunlight. The plant does not eat food like we do. In the animation scene s4 the roots are shown drinking water and minerals while the leaves make the food with sunlight, which shows the plant never eats food from the soil.
